summary: The note describes how the Catholic Church in Lesotho blends local culture into its worship. Many Christians there continue traditional cultural beliefs and rituals alongside Christianity. Hymn singing has taken on a local call-and-response style in Sesotho and English, and priests sometimes wear local dress during services.
one_line: Overview of how the Catholic Church in Lesotho incorporates local culture, music and dress into its services.
key_facts: Many Christians in Lesotho still practice their traditional cultural beliefs and rituals along with Christianity.
The Catholic Church in Lesotho has fused some aspects of local culture into its services.
Hymn singing in Lesotho Catholic services has developed into a local and traditional way of singing.
The local hymn style is a repetitive call and response style.
Hymns are sung in Sesotho, the indigenous language, as well as in English.
Sesotho is described in the note as the indigenous language of Lesotho.
Priests are seen dressed in local dress during services.
The note presents local dress worn by priests as part of the church's cultural adaptation.
